opening_message:
Ticket 1: Alexander Brown (employee ID E018) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E018.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Alexander Brown (E018) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write access; admin requires that the employee's role owns the system, and Analyst does not own Payroll. Therefore the maximum is write, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record (E018): contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: Note 1 says full_time (max write, since Analyst does not own Payroll), while Note 2 says contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never allowed). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive/least-privilege maximum: read. The requested admin exceeds that maximum, so grant read.

Note 1 (HR):
- role: Analyst
- employment type: full_time
- recommendation: write
- Reasoning: Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires role owns system, Analyst doesn't own Payroll. Max = write.

Note 2 (Security):
- role: Analyst (not looked up in own database)
- employment type: contractor
- security training: basic
- recommendation: read
- Reasoning: Contractor with basic training maxes out at read; admin never allowed. Max = read.

These notes conflict on employment type: full_time vs contractor. This matters a lot:
- If full_time: max is write (Analyst doesn't own Payroll, so no admin; full-time max is write). Requested admin > max write → grant write.
- If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin > max read → grant read.

Which note to trust? Note 1 (HR) says "looked up in own database before writing". Note 2 (Security) says employment type "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" - wait, actually note 2 says role is "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" but employment type is "contractor (looked up in own database before writing)". - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
- employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
